Never touch other directories (another agent is working in /home/ubuntu/english-only: it removes German and edits apps/web/src/messages/*, so keep your catalog edits minimal and local to the lines you must change). Read /home/ubuntu/policy/AGENTS.md first: strict rules (no code comments, no `as` assertions outside tests, explicit .ts extensions, all UI text from catalogs, ledger of lint/Effect overrides only shrinks). Do NOT commit, push, or use git write commands; leave changes uncommitted for me to review.

GOAL: product-policy numbers that appear in more than one place are stated exactly once, in `packages/domain/src/Policy.ts` (new, exported from the domain index), and every consumer derives from it. Motivation: the sign-in page said "expires in 5 minutes" while Better Auth and the email said 10; we already had to add a test tying `SIGN_IN_CODE_MINUTES` (domain/people/SignIn.ts) to `CODE_TTL_SECONDS` (packages/auth/src/options.ts). Make that class of bug impossible by construction.

DESIGN:
- `Policy.ts` exports a plain `as const`-style typed object (no Effect services, no Config: the browser app, email text and Better Auth setup all need these and not all run inside an Effect). Group it, e.g. `Policy.signIn = { codeMinutes: 10, codeLength: 6, codeAttempts: 5, magicLinkMinutes: 5, sessionDays: 30 }`, `Policy.text = { noteMaxLength: 2000, longTextMaxLength: 1000 }`, `Policy.backupRetentionDays = 30`, `Policy.testSend = { pollSeconds: 3, stalledMinutes: 5, giveUpMinutes: 15 }`. Plus small pure helpers if useful: `minutes(n)`, `days(n)` returning milliseconds/seconds, so no one writes `5 * 60_000` by hand. Use these exact current values; do not change any behavior or number.
- Make `@surveybeat/auth` depend on `@surveybeat/domain` (workspace:* in packages/auth/package.json, tsconfig project reference as other packages do, run `pnpm install` to update the lockfile). Check the lint plugin's boundary rules still allow it (domain must stay free of cloudflare/Alchemy/Foldkit). `packages/auth/src/options.ts`: `CODE_TTL_SECONDS`, `MAGIC_LINK_TTL_SECONDS`, `SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` derive from Policy; `otpLength` and `allowedAttempts` come from Policy.
- Delete `SIGN_IN_CODE_MINUTES` from domain/people/SignIn.ts and migrate all callers (apps/web App.ts, packages/cloudflare/src/auth/AuthResource.ts and its test) to Policy. Likewise migrate `NOTE_MAX_LENGTH` (domain/notes/Note.ts) and `LONG_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH` (domain/pulses/Question.ts) so their numbers live in Policy: either delete the old names and migrate every caller, or keep the old name only if it is a real schema/brand constant defined as `Policy.text.noteMaxLength` (prefer deleting; migrate callers and delete in the same change). The web `TEST_SEND_*` constants in apps/web/src/app/pulses.ts derive from Policy.testSend.
- Catalogs: strings that embed a policy number must take it as a placeholder so they cannot drift: apps/web catalog "signIn.sent" ("6-digit" -> `{digits}-digit`, minutes already `{minutes}`), "question.longText.help" (1,000), "note.count.one/.other" and "note.tooLong" (2,000; format with the locale's number formatting, e.g. Intl.NumberFormat, via the existing message helpers or pass a pre-formatted string), and the backup-retention "30 days" sentence (grep `30 days`). Update German (de.ts) placeholders to match only if de.ts still exists in your checkout (it does; the other agent deletes it later; just keep it compiling with the same placeholder names). Emails: packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts and AuthResource.ts texts take their numbers from Policy.
- Guard test (new, in packages/domain or apps/web messages tests, wherever catalog tests live): fail if any English catalog string in apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts or packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts contains a literal number followed by a unit matching /\b\d[\d,]*\s*(-digit|minutes?|hours?|days?|seconds?|characters?)\b/ unless it is on a short, explicit allowlist you document by key name in the test (e.g. keys with human-scale prose like "Still queued after 15 minutes" should become placeholders too if they are Policy values; truly unrelated prose can be allowlisted). Make the guard fail on a planted literal first, then remove the plant.
- Also grep other duplicated policy numbers you notice in non-test source (e.g. Retry.ts RETRY_WINDOW_MS/FIRST_RETRY_GAP_MS/MAX_RETRY_GAP_MS, Pulse.ts MIN/MAX/RECOMMENDED question and seconds limits, DEFAULT_MINIMUM_GROUP_SIZE, THEMES_LEASE_MS): only move one into Policy if it is used in more than one file/package or appears as a literal in a catalog. Leave single-use internal constants where they are. List in your report what you moved and what you deliberately left.

VALIDATE from /home/ubuntu/policy, fix until all pass: `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format` then `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:ledger`, `pnpm check:comments`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:privacy`, `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build`. No new lint disables or Effect diagnostic overrides. Don't run workerd adapter tests unless typecheck demands it.

REPORT: files changed/deleted, constants moved vs left (with reasons), anything you did differently from this brief, exact pass/fail counts per command.

## Changes

Nothing is committed, and no git write commands were run. All edits are in `/home/ubuntu/policy` (33 modified files, 1 new file, 0 deleted).

**New:** `packages/domain/src/Policy.ts` exports `Policy` (a plain `as const` object), the helpers `minutes(n)` and `days(n)` (both return milliseconds), and `toSeconds(ms)`. It is re-exported from the domain index. The answer entry imports it through a new subpath, `@surveybeat/domain/policy`, so it doesn't pull in the whole domain index.

**Domain:** `people/SignIn.ts` (`SIGN_IN_CODE_MINUTES` deleted), `notes/Note.ts` (`NOTE_MAX_LENGTH` deleted), `pulses/Question.ts` (`LONG_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH` deleted; it had no users), `privacy/Redaction.ts`, `pulses/Pulse.ts`, `pulses/Editor.ts`, `people/Team.ts`, `rounds/Themes.ts`, `package.json` (subpath export).

**Auth:** `packages/auth/package.json` and `tsconfig.json` (dependency and reference on domain), `src/options.ts` (TTLs, OTP length and attempts derive from Policy), `pnpm-lock.yaml` (3 lines, via `pnpm install --offline`).

**Cloudflare:** `auth/AuthResource.ts` and its test (email numbers from Policy), `auth/AuthHandlers.ts` (cookie max-age is `Duration.days(sessionDays)`), `Organization.ts` (trend window).

**Web app:** `app/App.ts`, `app/results.ts`, `app/pulses.ts` (test-send constants, copy params), `app/api.ts`, `app/directory.ts`, `app/components.ts` (privacy list now carries params), `site/render.ts` (landing copy takes params), `answer/main.ts` (textarea limit and disclosure), `messages/locale.ts` (new `formatNumber`, so "2,000" and "2.000" follow the locale).

**Catalogs:** `messages/catalog.ts`, `de.ts`, `answer.ts`, `answer.de.ts`. Placeholders added: `{digits}`, `{earliest}`, `{latest}`, `{max}`, `{minimum}`, `{perHour}`, `{days}`, `{groupSize}`, `{recommended}`, `{rounds}`, `{themes}`. Each substitution was count-checked, and the German placeholder names match the English ones.

**Guard tests:** `apps/web/src/messages/messages.test.ts` and `packages/emails/src/messages/messages.test.ts`. I planted `"Loading… 15 minutes"` in the English catalog and confirmed the guard failed on `app.loading`, then removed the plant and confirmed it passes.

## Constants moved vs left

**Moved into Policy:** `signIn` (code 10 min, 6 digits, 5 attempts, magic link 5 min, session 30 days), `text` (note 2000, long text 1000), `backupRetentionDays` 30, `testSend` (perHour 5, lifetime 7 days, poll 3 s, stalled 5 min, give-up 15 min), `groupSize` (default 4, minimum 3, maximum 100), `questions` (max 20, recommended 7), `sendWindow` (06:00 to 21:00), `themes.maximum` 5, `trendRounds` 12.

- The brief's three names are deleted: `SIGN_IN_CODE_MINUTES`, `NOTE_MAX_LENGTH` and `LONG_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH`.
- `testSendsPerHour`, `testInvitationLifetimeMs`, `DEFAULT_MINIMUM_GROUP_SIZE`, `MAX_QUESTIONS` and `MAX_THEMES` are kept as one-line aliases derived from Policy, to avoid touching many callers. The numbers live only in Policy.
- `RECOMMENDED_MAX_QUESTIONS`, `EARLIEST_SEND_TIME` and `LATEST_SEND_TIME` are deleted.

**Left in place, deliberately:**
- `RETRY_WINDOW_MS`, `FIRST_RETRY_GAP_MS`, `MAX_RETRY_GAP_MS` (Retry.ts): one production user, no catalog literal.
- `THEMES_LEASE_MS` (Organization.ts), `SendPolicy` lease and attempts (SendState.ts), `MIN_QUESTIONS`: single use.
- `RECOMMENDED_MAX_SECONDS` (90): one production file, shown through a parameter.
- `keptAnswersLifetimeMs` (365 days, answer/kept-answers.ts): one production file. This one is retention-related, so you may want a decision on it.
- `MIN_SUPPORTING_COMMENTS` (2): the site copy says "two" in words, which the digit guard cannot see.
- `ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS`, the auth `updateAge` of 24 h, the infra canary durations, unit conversions such as `/ 60_000`.
- Display scales ("Rating 1–5", "/ 5", "Label for 1/5"), the marketing mock data, and the singular "1-Round trend" label (allowlisted in the guard by key name).
- Test literals that restate numbers, such as `sign-in.test.ts` (`toBe(600)`) and the rendered-copy assertions in `App.scene.test.ts`.

## Deviations from the brief

1. **Guard regex is wider than the brief's.** It also matches `person(s)`, `people`, `questions`, `themes`, `rounds`, `tests`, is case-insensitive, and allows an optional hyphen (so "30-day" is caught). The brief's list alone would not catch "at least 4 people", which is a policy number. The guard covers units and these nouns only. It does not catch bare numbers, so `two` and the scale labels are outside its reach.
2. **The guard is in two files,** because neither the web app nor the emails package can import the other's catalog. The regex and the allowlist logic are duplicated.
3. **Catalog scope is larger than the brief listed.** The "literal in a catalog" rule pulled in group-size copy, question limits, the themes maximum and the trend window, across the landing page as well as the app. Each of these is a placeholder.
4. **Effect Durations for the poll interval and cookie.** `TEST_SEND_POLL_INTERVAL` is `Duration.seconds(...)`, and the cookie max-age is `Duration.days(...)`. Template-literal strings widen to `string`, and Effect rejects that under `Duration.Input`.
